subject: math
intro: Ms. Chen again. Let's plan an 8th grade lesson that applies the Pythagorean theorem to real-world problems.

beats.narration: The title promises real-world use, which answers "when will we ever use this?"
beats.text: Missing Sides: Pythagoras in the Real World

beats.narration: This standard is about applying the theorem to find unknown side lengths in real-world problems.
Focused on application, since they proved the theorem earlier in the unit.
beats.text: Students will be able to apply the Pythagorean theorem to find a missing side length of a right triangle in real-world and two-dimensional contexts.

beats.narration: Most students don't know TVs are measured on the diagonal, so it's a great surprise.
beats.text: "Will a 55-inch TV fit on a 48-inch wide entertainment center?" Students discuss what "55-inch" actually measures.

beats.narration: Finding a leg is the step where students most often add instead of subtract, so I model it on purpose.
beats.text: Model identifying the right triangle and the hypotenuse in a picture, then solve the TV problem. Do a second example finding a leg (a ladder against a wall).

beats.narration: Measuring to check shows the theorem really works.
beats.text: Around-the-school measuring: groups measure two sides of real right triangles (a ramp, a door diagonal) with tape measures, calculate the third, then measure to check.

beats.narration: This finds a leg, which is the trickier case.
beats.text: A 13-foot ladder reaches 12 feet up a wall. How far is the base from the wall? Show your work.

outro: A hook that surprises, two models, real measurement. Your turn.
